observation.visible_scene: A low-angle view of a grassy field bordered by a dark tree line under a pale dusk/dawn sky. A large, intensely bright fireball dominates the left half of the frame, casting a strong orange-yellow glow across the grass in the foreground.
visible_changes: The bright white-yellow mass on the left grows larger and rises vertically over the sequence, its core shifting from mid-frame toward the upper-left edge.
As it rises, the smooth white blob develops visible turbulent flame texture, transitioning from pure white to yellow and orange lobes.
A vertical column/stem of glowing orange light and haze forms beneath the rising mass, connecting the fireball to a bright patch at ground level on the left.
The foreground grass lighting changes from a washed-out yellow-green (frame 1) to a deeper red-orange (later frames) as the white core moves upward and away.
The top of the fireball begins to drift partly out of the upper frame edge in the final frames while the ground-level stem remains visible.
The tree line and horizon stay in fixed positions, indicating the apparent motion is the fireball rising, not camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What produced or ignited the fireball is not shown.
Whether the fireball continues to rise, dissipates, or falls after the last frame is unknown.
The state of the scene before t=0 (the mass is already fully formed and bright at the first frame).
uncertain_details: Minor camera shake cannot be ruled out, but the static background suggests no deliberate pan/zoom.
The vertical column could be a light trail, heated haze, or smoke; its exact nature is not determinable from the frames alone.
The boundary between the bright core and the surrounding glow is partly saturated, making precise shape tracking uncertain.
